title: Interval DP: Matrix Chain Multiplication
contract: Dimension array d describes matrices d[i] × d[i+1]. Find the minimum scalar multiplication count; at least one matrix and positive dimensions, result fits long.
optimal: int n=d.length-1;long[][] dp=new long[n][n];for(int length=2;length<=n;length++)for(int l=0;l+length<=n;l++){int r=l+length-1;dp[l][r]=Long.MAX_VALUE;for(int k=l;k<r;k++)dp[l][r]=Math.min(dp[l][r],dp[l][k]+dp[k+1][r]+(long)d[l]*d[k+1]*d[r+1]);emit("Choose the final split after solving shorter intervals","interval",new int[]{l,r},"costs",dp);}return dp[0][n-1];
reasoning: Each possible final split creates two smaller matrix chains; recursively enumerate all splits.
dp[l][r] stores the optimal multiplication count for the closed interval of matrices.
Fill by increasing interval length so both split subchains are ready. Multiplication cost depends on d[l], d[k+1], and d[r+1], a common indexing trap.
